cim: Rep. George Whitesides leads new bipartisan House artificial intelligence caucus
cim_eredeti: Rep. George Whitesides leads new bipartisan House artificial intelligence caucus
szoveg_eredeti:
Rep. George Whitesides, a Democrat from Los Angeles County, just reelected to a second term, will co-chair a new bipartisan caucus focused on addressing artificial intelligence safety and security risks while maintaining the United States’ role as a global leader in AI technologies.

Members of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus intend to advance legislation and policies that include targeted guardrails, engage with AI experts and industry leaders and equip Congress to act quickly to respond to emerging risks and major incidents while also supporting innovation.

Artificial intelligence — which at times has gone rogue — is advancing more swiftly than ever, and Congress must keep pace in terms of taking action, Whitesides, D-Agua Dulce, said in a statement.

“Now is the time to build bipartisan consensus and advance commonsense guardrails we know will reduce the most serious risks,” he said.

“Americans are rightly concerned about where this technology is heading, but too often the debate in Washington is framed as a choice between doing nothing and banning AI altogether. That’s a false choice,” he added. “We have an opportunity to pursue smart, targeted solutions that protect the public while allowing American innovation to thrive.”

Whitesides will co-chair the caucus alongside Reps. Don Beyer, a Democrat from Virginia, and Nathaniel Moran, a Republican from Texas.

Other caucus members include Reps. Ted Lieu and Brad Sherman, Democrats from L.A. County, and Jay Obernolte, a Republican from San Bernardino County, along with 20 other House members.

Lieu, D-Torrance, and Obernolte, R-Hesperia, previously co-chaired a House task force on artificial intelligence.

The launch of this caucus comes at a time when public confidence in AI has been shaken by recent security incidents.

In July, ChatGPT maker OpenAI acknowledged its AI system, acting on its own, hacked into another AI company. Later that month, Anthropic said its AI models hacked into three companies during testing.

And exit polling during the midterm elections, conducted by NBC News and other news organizations, found that AI and data centers were a crucial or major factor in voters’ choice for Congress 56% of the time.

The poll also found that 43% of respondents, a plurality, felt neither major political party was better at dealing with AI issues.
